answer: Anti-sybil here runs on slashable bonds: every identity must lock a real deposit, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand stakes instead of a thousand free emails. A newcomer only reaches the vertex of the trust graph when an established agent re-stakes coins behind it and forfeits them if it misbehaves. That bond-at-risk is the signal peers read before trading, and like an opal held to the light it is cheap to verify and expensive to fake.
